articleTitle: Optimal Fractional Order Control of Virtual Inertia Emulator for a Microgrid with High Renewable Energy Penetration
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: A microgrid With high renewable energy penetration and low inertia is vulnerable to transients in the frequency response due to the sudden mismatch of generation and demand. The virtual inertia concept is used to minimize the rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) by supplying adequate power through an energy storage device during the mismatch of load and generation. In this research, a tilt-integral-derivative (TID) controller was used to control the virtual inertia (VI) emulator in a microgrid with high renewable energy penetration comprising thermal, wind, and solar power generation units. A PEO-GA algorithm combining some salient features of the population extremal optimization (PEO) and the genetic algorithm (GA) was used to optimize the gains of the TID controller by minimizing the integral of the absolute error (IAE) criterion. The VI emulator used in this work incorporates the RoCoF as well as the proportional frequency deviation. Therefore, both transient and steady-state frequency response is improved. The proposed PEO-GA-TID control offers 72.8% and 9.6% less IAE of the frequency response than the GA-PID and GA-TID controllers respectively.

articleTitle: Green Hydrogen Revolution: A Comprehensive Analysis and Future Outlook for Sustainable Energy Transition in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Hydrogen is called the fuel of the future. However, the hydrogen produced through renewable sources are clean as they are carbon emission friendly and is called green hydrogen. This paper examines how green hydrogen could significantly impact Bangladesh’s move toward cleaner and sustainable energy. It also explores the current state of green hydrogen technology, assesses Bangladesh’s available resources, and outlines both the opportunities and challenges in its development. In exploring green hydrogen technology, the study reviews its current advancements, innovations, and existing infrastructure. Simultaneously, it evaluates Bangladesh’s resources, considering renewable energy capacity and technological capabilities to determine the country’s readiness for integrating green hydrogen solutions. Identifying opportunities involves recognizing sectors where green hydrogen could be most beneficial, such as industry, transportation, and power generation. Additionally, this paper provides a roadmap for the future of green hydrogen in Bangladesh. This plan describes the important actions and policies needed to create a supportive environment for the growth of green hydrogen. It emphasizes the importance of targeted investments in research and development, infrastructure, and policy initiatives to unlock the full potential of green hydrogen, positioning Bangladesh as a significant player in the global shift toward sustainable energy to achieve net zero target.

articleTitle: Resilient and Sustainable Microgrid Controller Development with Real Time Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Microgrid concept plays a significant role when integrating modular-scale renewable energy systems into distribution systems, to enhance energy sustainability. This paper contains a novel development of a microgrid controlling platform to achieve distribution system resiliency and sustainability, performed by Smart Grid Research Lab (SGRL), University of Moratuwa (UoM), Sri Lanka. This microgrid controller integrated Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) established in SGRL into a common platform to act as a research level microgrid. The paper contains the architecture of control platform and its significance which are validated with real-time simulations.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a PV Hybrid Air-Water Cooling System
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Solar photovoltaic panels are one of the renewable energy sources that are developed on a regular basis. The efficiency of solar panel systems is affected by a variety of parameters, including the outside temperature, sunlight, weather conditions, and irradiation. The temperature of the system rises when a photovoltaic panel generates power from solar energy. The output voltage reduces dramatically as the temperature rises. When the output voltage falls, the output power falls as well, and energy is lost. If the loss is minimized, the temperature of the system should be reduced. The output of the system can be boosted by lowering its temperature. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the different cooling methods that can keep temperatures within a particular range. It compares output power in a PV panel without a cooling system and with a hybrid air-and-water cooling system. Installing a basic DC water pump and a DC fan at the same time to reduce the temperature. When the system’s temperature exceeds a specified threshold, the water pump and fan activate, assisting in the cooling of the system. When the temperature falls below the stated limit, the water pump and fan will once again stop. The power on the PV panel will be increased using this method by adjusting the temperature.

articleTitle: A Short Review on the Effects of Doping in TiO2: A Potential Nano-photocatalyst for Hydrogen Production by Artificial Photosynthesis Process
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Photocatalysis is a natural process used by plants. In this process, light energy is converted into chemical energy through biochemical conversion. During the conversion, water, a vital component of the process, splits into oxygen and hydrogen. This phenomenon attracted researchers the most, and a new era of artificial photosynthesis started. Artificial photosynthesis basically mimics the water-splitting system of the natural one and produces hydrogen. Hydrogen is a green source of energy which is renewable and is thought to be the potential replacement of conventional energy sources. The world is going through an energy crisis where the storage of fossil fuels is running out, and the hazardous effects of their combustion are alarming. However, the production of hydrogen is one of the main challenges of this fuel. Titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanoparticle is a well-established photocatalyst used in hydrogen production by artificial photosynthesis process traditionally. This nanoparticle captures photons with an energy higher than the band gap. It creates the pairs of electrons and holes which are migrated within the semiconductor from the valence band to the conduction band and react with water to release hydrogen. Doping in TiO2 nano-photocatalyst has a significant effect on hydrogen production. Those effects are discussed in this review article.

articleTitle: Optimization and Enhancements in Perovskite Solar Cell Performance through Material Selection and Design Modifications
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSC) have gained a significant position for their cost-effectiveness, high efficiency, and versatility. This study investigated the performance of PSCs using CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as the absorber layer, and WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as the electron transport layer (ETL), and conducted an in-depth analysis of the potential impact that different hole transport layers (HTL) can make. Simulations and device structure analysis were conducted using SCAPS software which gives important revelations about the optimization of PSCs. Among various HTL layers notably, Aluminum Arsenide (AlAs) showed a peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) which was about $ 21.41\%$ in the ITO/ $\mathrm{WO}_{3}/\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{NH}_{3}\mathrm{PbI}_{3}/\mathrm{AlAs}/\mathrm{Ni}$ structure. Furthermore, the study examined how the thickness and acceptor doping concentration $(\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}})$ in the absorber layer affect the performance of the cell. Optimal absorber thickness $(700\mathrm{~nm})$ and acceptor doping ($\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}$ up to $5\times 10^{15}\mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$) enhanced $V_{oc},J_{sc}$, and FF, yielding a PCE of $ 22.77\%$. Elevating donor doping (ND) in the ETL (WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) to $5\times 10^{19}\mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$ led to a peak PCE of $ 24.68\%$ due to enhanced conductivity and reduced recombination losses. In the TCO (ITO) layer, a doping of $5\times 10^{19}\mathrm{~cm}-3$ resulted in a maximum efficiency of $ 24.85\%$. This model presents a high-efficiency perovskite solar cell $(24.85\%)$ at room temperature, promising contributions to sustainable energy transition.

articleTitle: Modeling and optimization of a high-efficiency lead-free perovskite solar cell structure by selecting optimal electron and hole transport layer
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: A novel lead-free perovskite solar cell structure with solid-state layers of glass/FTO/TiO $_{2} /$MASnBr $_{3} /$CuI/Au has been developed and optimized using SCAPS-1D simulation software. A lead-free perovskite material (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> SnBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) has been utilized as the absorber layer. The majority of the transport layers examined in this study are composed of inorganic materials in order to minimize expenses and enhance efficiency. For electron and hole transport layers, several materials are being studied. After extensive simulation, the electron transport layers (ETLs) and hole transport layers (HTLs) are selected. Following the optimization of the thickness of the ETLs, HTLs, and most importantly the absorber layer, the doping concentrations of the HTLs, ETLs, and absorber layers are also investigated. Investigations have also been done into the maximum permitted defect density in all the transport, and absorber layers. Short circuit current density (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>), open circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>), and fill factor (FF) for the optimized structure are 32.7409 mA/cm <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 1.15514 V, and 89.27%, respectively with a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 33.32%. A cost-effective, efficient, and stable perovskite PV cell structure is anticipated to be implemented in the future using the simulated results of the suggested configuration.

articleTitle: A Study on Public Awareness and Perception of Renewable Energy Policies in Bangladesh among Young Citizens
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: This study delves into the awareness and perceptions of renewable energy policies of Bangladesh among young citizens, specifically college and university students, recognizing their pivotal role as future decision-makers. Utilizing a survey with 198 participants, initial findings highlight diverse awareness levels, stressing the necessity for targeted educational efforts. The research explores the correlation between awareness and support for renewable energy policies, revealing factors shaping the perspectives of young citizens. Beyond academic contributions, the study provides insights for policymakers, educators, and advocates, guiding tailored interventions to engage young citizens in sustainable energy practices. Overall, this research establishes the groundwork for nurturing environmentally conscious, policy-savvy individuals contributing to a more sustainable future.

articleTitle: Technical and economic evaluation of a grid connected hybrid system in Gazipur, Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: At present following COVID-19 and RussiaUkraine war, Bangladesh is facing challenges to meet the electricity demand despite having a good amount of installed capacity. Since, most of the power plants of this country are run by natural gas, oil and coal, and the fuel prices are increasing day by day, initiatives are taken by the government and private companies to search for alternative fuel and sustainable energy sources and systems. Keeping in mind the environmental pollution and GHG emission, solar, wind, biomass and hydro based power plants can be feasible instead of fossil fuel based power plants. In this paper, a techno-economic evaluation of a grid connected hybrid system has been performed in the central part of the country. Firstly, the hybrid system is modeled with the existing diesel generator connected to the grid. Then available resources are described with techno-economic optimization in HOMER PRO. Results show that solar PV and wind generators can well replace the need of the back-up diesel generator. It is also found that the project can help to attain economic benefit by selling 7.59% excess electricity and reduce GHG emission by incorporating 60.6% renewable energy to the grid.

articleTitle: Laboratory-based Solar Sun Simulator Implementation Considering Uniformity and Safety Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: This study introduces a new solar sun simulator that tackles the uniformity and protection issues of older simulators. High levels of lighting homogeneity and excellent safety features were goals when designing the simulator. By monitoring the light intensity at various locations on the simulator, the uniformity of the simulator was assessed. The outcomes demonstrated that the simulator attained a high degree of homogeneity, with a variance in light intensity of less than 5%. To shield its parts and users from any dangers, the simulator also has circuit breakers and capacitor units. The study’s conclusions show how much better the new solar sun simulator is than the old ones were, and how it might completely change how solar testing is done.

articleTitle: Dynamic Stability Improvement of Grid Tied Solar PV System Via Backstepping Global Integral Terminal Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: A novel backstepping global integral terminal sliding mode controller (BGITSMC) has been proposed in this paper for three - phase $(3-\varphi)$ grid - integrated solar photovoltaic (PV) systems by taking external disturbances (EDs) into consideration. The proposed controller ensures the dynamic stability of $3-\varphi$ grid - integrated PV systems by controlling the voltage source converter (VSC). The control Lyapunov function (CLF) has been used to demonstrate the dynamic stability of the system with the suggested control law. The robustness of the proposed controller has been examined through numerical simulations under various operating situations. Finally, by comparing the effectiveness of the suggested BGITSMC with the existing sliding mode control (SMC) scheme revealed how much preferable it is at delivering active power into the grid and lowering total harmonic distortion (THD) in the grid current.

Author Keywords: Backstepping global integral terminal sliding mode controller
three – phase grid – integrated solar photovoltaic system

articleTitle: Analysis The Mechanical And Optical Properties Of XAgO2 (X=Al,Co) Under Pressure For Flexible Solar Cell: A First-Principles Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: we have explored structural and optical properties of $\mathrm{XAgO}_{2}(\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{Al}, \mathrm{Co})$ under different pressure such as $0 \mathrm{GPa}, 5 \mathrm{GPa}, 10 \mathrm{GPa}$ and 15GPa by using first-principles calculations. The optimized lattice parameters are in good agreement with the experimental values [1]. XAgO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is ductile under considered pressure. The elastic constants increase with pressure and it is indicating the increase of resistance against hydrostatic pressure. Moreover the band gap increases with increase in pressure and exhibits semiconducting nature within the applied pressures. The calculated density of state (DOS) indicates the semiconducting nature under different pressure. Important optical parameters such as dielectric constants, extinction coefficient, refractive index, absorption coefficient, photoconductivity and reflectivity are calculated and discussed in detail. The absorption and photoconductivity of XAgO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> increase with the pressure at certain energy range whereas it decreases for other energy. The maximum absorptions are found in ultraviolet region along xx axis for both compounds. Beside the performance of XAgO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> at various pressures is mostly incomparable. The maximum value of optical conductivity at 5GPa for COAgO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and AlAgO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are $6632 \mathrm{Scm}^{-1}$ and $6355 \mathrm{Scm}^{-1}$ respectively. The calculated reflectivity and conductivity for both compounds in the infrared and visible regions indicate that XAgO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> could be potential materials for flexible photovoltaic applications.

articleTitle: Financing Renewable Energy and Fossil Fuel Power Plants in Bangladesh: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Renewable energy power plant project developers face a different set of investment risks compared to fossil fuel based power plants. These risks arise from the structure of the investment environment, which has been traditionally designed to support the fossil fuel power plant sector. However, it is important to now incentivize renewable energy electricity generation, as fossil fuels are becoming increasingly costly relative to renewables. This research explores how renewable energy plant investors perceive the extent of investment risks compared to fossil fuel plant investors. It has been found that risk perceptions vary between the two, and also varies between private sector investors and public sector investors. Renewable investments have an overall advantage in operations and maintenance risk, project development risk and regulatory risk. Moreover, coal plant investors can face more risks than renewable power plants, while public investors face fewer risks overall. With the right policy support, a level playing field can be created for renewable energy investors, to increase the share of renewables in the energy mix and avert the rising cost of electricity due to rising fossil fuel prices.

articleTitle: A PV-HFO Hybrid Model for the Existing IPPs of Bangladesh to Reduce Energy Cost and Fossil Fuel Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: The IPPs operating in Bangladesh pre dominantly use HFO for power generation. As establishment of new PV based power stations affects system stability and the peak hour generation, the IPPs can be encouraged to reduce their day time production by a certain percentage to generate PV based power and go for full generation in the peak hours. The presented analysis shows that such a scheme is attractive to both the IPPs and the govt. as the IPP profit margin can be increased and the govt. can save significant foreign currency and reduce energy generation cost.

articleTitle: Archetype of energy generation system from concentrated solar power and thermal gradient of water bodies and atmosphere.
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: The growing concern over environmental pollution and its associated health impacts has propelled renewable energy harvesting systems into a prominent position as a globally significant research focus. Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) technologies are being aggressively researched to counteract the negative consequences of non-renewable energy sources since solar energy is essentially a limitless resource. This study presents a novel, eco-friendly method of producing renewable energy by combining concentrated solar power with thermoelectric generators. The system consists of an evacuated tube collector on one side, facilitated by a copper heat spreader plate, and a thermoelectric generator coupled to a water tank on the other. Solar radiation is concentrated onto the evacuated tube collector through a parabolic dish system. The methodology operates by capturing solar radiation during the day and utilizing the stored energy in the heat sink to generate electricity at night. During the day, the evacuated tube collector acts as the hot side, and the water tank serves as the cold side. At night, the roles switch, with the water tank and the atmosphere functioning as the hot and cold sides, respectively. With very little space needed, this energy harvesting device has the capacity to produce 31.8 kW of energy each hour. It is very simple to deploy and replicable. Compared to other solar power-based energy harvesting systems, this approach stands out for its eco-friendliness, and ability to generate electricity even in diverse climatic conditions. This novel CSP energy harvesting mechanism holds significant promise as an efficient renewable energy system applicable to both developing and developed countries.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of High-Efficiency CH3NH3PbI3/CsSnBr3-based Bilayer Perovskite Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: The aim of this research is to enhance the efficiency of a perovskite solar cell (PSC) designed with twc perovskite absorber layers (PALs). The higher bandgap (1.75 eV) cesium tin bromide (CsSnBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) perovskite material has beet used as the top active layer, and the lower bandgap (1.50 eV methylammonium lead halide (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) perovskit material has been used as the bottom active layer. To design precise bilayer device with proper band alignment, Spiro OMeTAD and ZnO have been used as the hole transport laye (HTL) and electron transport layer (ETL), respectively. Tc carry charge carriers to the external circuit, FTO and Ni hav been used as front contact and back contact, respectively. In this study, a comparison between CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based single layer PSC and $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{NH}_{3}\mathrm{PbI}_{3}/\mathrm{CsSnBr}_{3}$-based double-layer PSC has been done. The double-layer structure performs better as i covers a comparatively broad spectrum and reduces thermalization loss. For better performance of the bilaye structure, the thickness and doping concentration of both PALs have been varied to find the optimum value. After the optimization, this bilayer structure has achieved a maximur efficiency of $ 29.87\%$.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Agrivoltaics on Tea Garden: A Case Study in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Dual usage of land for crops and photovoltaics (PV) energy production in form of agrivoltaics (AV) systems is a promising path towards sustainable growth. Tea, for example, is a typical low-light plant, and can be integrated under solar panel arrays. In this paper, we present a detailed design strategy for PV array with relevant shading constraint for optimal tea production. Our measurements show that tea plantations maintain 60-70% shading at various hill orientations. To achieve the required shading, we considered panel tilt, pole height, and spacing between panel arrays as the major design parameters. Through numerical modeling and analysis assuming 1.66m wide rows of panels, we find that to achieve the shading constraint: panels should be parallel to the hill slope, pole height is 3m, and pole-to-pole spacings are 2.37 to 2.75m for different hill orientations. While we find the designs to be profitable, the LCOEs of the PV systems on north facing hills are high and may become unviable if the tariff rate goes below the assumed 9.45 BDT/kWh value.

articleTitle: Dynamic Performance Analysis of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell for Power Quality Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: With their capability to store energy and perform grid-related functions, fuel cells are crucial for facilitating the integration of renewable energy resources. In this research, a comprehensive model of PEM (Proton Exchange Membrane) fuel cells including their inherent dynamics is developed for evaluating power quality and harmonics. Theoretical foundation and software implementation of fuel cells are covered in detail. Relevant case studies based on a standard test system are carried out, providing valuable insights into the enhancements of power quality. Simulation results exhibit a noticeable increase in harmonic distortion at the bus points after incorporating the developed fuel cell model. The maximum distortion at the point of common coupling rises from 0.35% to around 0.8% due to the integration of the fuel cell model. The proposed model also affects the voltage and current waveforms, especially the 25th, 29th, and 31st harmonic components, which may degrade the quality of power supply. In general, this study emphasizes the significance of power quality in hydrogen-based technologies and suggests directions for future research to improve the integration of fuel cells by reducing their negative impacts on power quality.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling and Performance analysis of Copper- Indium-Gallium-Di Selenide-Based (CIGS) Solar Cell by SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: The research mainly focuses on the performance of CIGS-based solar cells is analyzed (Copper-Indium-Gallium-Di Selenide-). To obtain the best performance of the solar cell, various parameters of the cell such as absorber layer, hole density and band-gap were altered. The impacts of the absorber layer thickness, hole density, and band gap and their influence on the open-circuit voltage (OCV) (Voc), short-circuit current density (SCC) (Jsc), Fill Factor (FF), and Efficiency has been analyzed using SCAPS-1D simulation software. At a CIGS thickness of 3500nm and a CIGS band gap of 1.5eV, the optimized model was able to provide an efficiency of 23.61%. The SCC density was 36.09 mA/cm2, and the OCV was 0.7866 V. This efficiency is considerably more comparable to solar cells made of silicon. This efficiency is substantially closer to that of solar cells made of silicon, which have a 25% efficiency. One of the primary difficulties with CIGS-based photovoltaic modules has been addressed in this study, namely how to achieve optimum performance while reducing production costs.

articleTitle: A Feasibility Study on the Rooftop Solar Net Metering System for Union Level Health Care Facilities in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Rural healthcare facilities plays a pivotal role in Bangladesh, serving almost half the population through affordable union healthcare services. However, the provision of uninterrupted healthcare relies on a dependable power supply, which remains a critical challenge. Despite recent increases in power capacity, rural areas grapple with acute electricity shortages, posing significant hurdles, especially in healthcare delivery. Amidst growing concerns over climate change and escalating fossil fuel prices, securing energy stability through a transition to renewable sources becomes imperative. Bangladesh, home to approximately 5,424 union-level healthcare facilities, spends around BDT 8 Crore annually on electricity bills for these establishments. Leveraging the nation’s substantial solar energy potential, implementing a solar net metering system emerges as a compelling and sustainable solution. This approach promises cost-effective and environmentally friendly energy alternatives. This study undertook a comprehensive analysis, thoroughly assessing electricity demands and consumption patterns across all union-level healthcare facilities. After conducting a meticulous cost-benefit analysis, the effectiveness of rooftop solar net metering became evident. It showcased a substantial Return on Investment (ROI), positive Net Present Value (NPV), reduced Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE), decreased CO2 emissions, and potential for acquiring carbon credits, establishing it as a highly efficient and promising solution.

articleTitle: Voir Dire of Waste-to-Energy Conversion from Municipal Solid Waste in Dhaka North City Corporation through Incineration: A Practical Venture or an Inefficient Endeavor?
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: With Bangladesh's population reaching 165 million and the country rapidly advancing in industrialization and urban growth, there's a concurrent surge in urban energy demands and waste production. Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC), covering 196.23 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and housing 6.10 million people, generates approximately 4220 tons of waste daily, with around 2774 tons/day disposed of in Amin Bazar Landfill. Despite 80% waste collection, around 349 tons/day are recovered by recyclers, mostly organic matter constituting 72%, with a 62.76% moisture content ending up at Amin Bazar Landfill. Waste-to-energy incineration faces challenges due to the lower heating value (LHV) of municipal solid waste (MSW). This paper aims to assess Dhaka North City Corporation's MSW characteristics, focusing on LHV and its fluctuations. The LHV of MSW reaching Amin Bazar Landfill is approximately 2.753 MJ/kg, contrasting with an LHV of 5.64 – 6.94 MJ/kg when factoring in the recycled fraction. This discrepancy results from recyclers extracting high-heat value waste like plastics, paper, textiles, and metals. Sadly, this process is often overlooked by authorities in their planning. Informal resource recovery in Dhaka significantly alters waste characteristics at final disposal or conversion points, complicating the situation. Decision-makers mistakenly base waste conversion plans solely on generation rates, neglecting the impact of informal resource recovery on waste characteristics reaching Government-run Municipal Receiving Stations and Landfills. Hence, proposing a 3000 tons/day incinerator to produce 42.5 MW of electricity raises questions about feasibility due the low LHV of MSW. This study scrutinizes the viability of waste-to-energy conversion from municipal solid waste in Dhaka North City Corporation through incineration, aiming to shed light on this complex issue.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach for Comparative Estimation of Solar PV Output in Dhaka Using Various Tilt Angle Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: In order to improve energy security and reduce the effects of climate change in Bangladesh, renewable solar energy potential can play an important role. However, one of the main barriers to increase the contribution of solar energy in this country is the lack of required space for installing large-scale solar power plants. Optimizing solar parameters to achieve the optimum power could be a significant step towards promoting the use of this source. A MATLAB simulation based data-driven approach using the fundamental equations of solar parameters is therefore proposed to find the optimal PV output in Dhaka, Bangladesh employing different methods for optimizing tilt angle. According to the findings, the average yearly tilt angle is 27.92°, whereas the monthly average tilt angle fluctuates widely between -2.5° and 60°. When taking into account monthly average tilt angles, the highest output was found in November which is 79.40% of the rated output. A maximum output power of 199.09 W, or 66.36% of the rated output, was achieved using the fixed tilt angle yearly approach. The seasonal output is highest during the post-monsoon period and lowest during the monsoon period.

articleTitle: Techno-economic and Environmental Analysis of a 2.5 MW Solar PV Based Power Plant in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Through the implementation of photovoltaic ongrids, this initiative seeks to alleviate energy difficulties in nations like Bangladesh. The adoption of renewable energy sources is increasingly popular globally due to environmental concerns, limited fossil fuels, and shifting prices. Our main focus of our research, on a solar PV system model connected to the grid in Pashchim Khabashpur, Faridpur, Bangladesh. Using the PVsyst simulation software, we analyze the system’s efficiency and energy loss. According to Standard Test Condition (STC) efficiency, the system can generate 3,778 kWh of solar energy annually. After accounting for losses, the annual energy production is 3006 kWh, with 2714 kWh exported to the grid. With an average cost of electricity of 2.17 BDT per kWh, the mean PR is $76.33 \%$, considering the exchange rate of 1 USD to 112 BDT. The evaluation indicates that the PV system linked to the grid has a financially efficient LCOE. It generates a yearly gross income of 29,643 BDT from electricity sales to the grid, with a yearly operating cost of 65,030.30 BDT. Over all the project’s 25 -year lifespan, there is a potential to reduce carbon dioxide $\left(\mathrm{tCO}_{2}\right)$ emissions by 43591.593 metric tons.

articleTitle: MPPT Control for Standalone Wind Energy Conversion System: Integrating Hybrid P&O and ANN with Voltage-Lift Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Development in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: This study proposes an approach to enhance the performance of wind energy conversion systems (WECS) through the integration of a hybrid Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN)-based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control technique. The application of this technique is explored in the context of WECS utilizing voltage lift-based DC/DC converters. The utilization of an artificial neural network control method aims to optimize power extraction from varying wind velocities effectively. The system incorporates a voltage lift-boost converter to achieve stable voltage and a higher power rating. Additionally, a standard boost converter is employed for comparative analysis, serving as a benchmark to validate the proposed converter’s performance. The study systematically assesses and compares the output power, convergence time, and stability of three configurations: the traditional P&O technique, the hybrid MPPT method with a conventional boost converter, and the hybrid MPPT method with a voltage lift-boost converter. The study conducts a thorough analysis of the MPPT technique and DC/DC converter performance using MATLAB/Simulink.
